14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324:

326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown

348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]

353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]

359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale

371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |

384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

21: 
22: ### Location & Naming

25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95:

98: ```markdown

100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes

109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

245: - Root cause analysis required

253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

20:

22:

36: ### Acceptance Standard
37: 
38: **[P0] Rust output must be byte-for-byte identical to the pinned TypeScript oracle for every migrated behavior and every shipped boundary.**
39: 
40: ```rust
41: pub fn assert_byte_parity(
42:     typescript_bytes: &[u8],
43:     rust_bytes: &[u8],
44: ) {
45:     assert_eq!(rust_bytes, typescript_bytes);
46: }
47: ```

50: 
51: ### Numeric Contracts
52: 
53: **[P0] Preserve each TypeScript numeric operation independently.** These operations are not interchangeable:
54: 
55: ```typescript
56: Number(value.toFixed(6))
57: Math.round(value * 1_000_000) / 1_000_000
58: value.toFixed(6)
59: ```

62:

64: - **[P0]** Do not assume Rust `round` matches JavaScript `Math.round`, especially for negative halfway values.
65: - **[P0]** Do not assume `f64::to_string`, `ryu`, or `serde_json` matches JavaScript number spelling.
66: - **[P0]** Handle `-0.0` according to the oracle.
67: - **[P0]** Reject or encode non-finite values exactly as TypeScript does.
68: - **[P0]** Do not introduce `mul_add` without fixtures proving unchanged rounding.
69: - **[P0]** Avoid platform-variable transcendental operations unless quantized and cross-target tested.
70: 
71: ```rust
72: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
73: pub enum QuantizeError {
74:     #[error("value must be finite")]
75:     NonFinite,
76: 
77:     #[error("quantized value is outside the supported range")]
78:     OutOfRange,
79: }
80: 
81: pub fn quantize_math_round_six(
82:     value: f64,
83: ) -> Result<f64, QuantizeError> {
84:     if !value.is_finite() {
85:         return Err(QuantizeError::NonFinite);
86:     }
87: 
88:     let scaled = value * 1_000_000.0;
89:     let rounded = (scaled + 0.5).floor();
90:     let result = rounded / 1_000_000.0;
91: 
92:     if !result.is_finite() {
93:         return Err(QuantizeError::OutOfRange);
94:     }
95: 
96:     Ok(result)
97: }

103: 
104: **[P0] Every observable sort requires a complete comparator ending in a deterministic unique key.** This protects **ranking and serialized-order parity**.

108: 
109: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]

111:     pub id: String,
112:     pub score: FiniteScore,
113:     pub source_priority: u32,
114: }

117:     candidates: &mut [RankedCandidate],
118: ) {

120:         right
121:             .score
122:             .get()
123:             .total_cmp(&left.score.get())
124:             .then_with(|| {
125:                 left.source_priority.cmp(&right.source_priority)
126:             })
127:             .then_with(|| left.id.cmp(&right.id))
128:     });
129: }

147: - Field order
148: - Delimiters
149: - Missing-value representation

163: ) -> String {

165:     let digest = Sha256::digest(preimage.as_bytes());
166:     let hexadecimal = hex::encode(digest);

176: - **[P0]** Do not change hash libraries without byte-level fixtures.
177: - **[P0]** Do not truncate before encoding when the oracle truncates after encoding.

180:

182: - **[P0]** Do not expose filesystem enumeration order.
183: - **[P0]** Do not expose database row order without an explicit complete ordering.
184: - **[P0]** Do not expose graph insertion order unless it is contractual.
185: - **[P0]** Do not expose thread or task completion order.

198: - Number spelling
199: - String escaping
200: - UTF-8 encoding
201: - Newline policy
202: - Trailing newline behavior
203: - Array order

210: - **[P1]** Provide diagnostic structural diffs in addition to the authoritative byte diff.

213:

215: |------|-------------------|----------|
216: | TypeScript oracle | Pinned commit and generated expected bytes | P0 |
217: | Pure Rust core | Golden replay | P0 |
218: | napi-rs native addon | Packaged artifact load and golden replay | P0 |
219: | wasm-bindgen | Built artifact load and golden replay | P0 |
220: | napi-rs WASI fallback | Forced fallback load and golden replay | P0 |
221: | Sidecar | Packaged executable protocol replay | P0 |

233: - **[P0]** Golden expected output must be generated by TypeScript, never authored by Rust.
234: - **[P0]** CI must never automatically accept changed golden output.

239: - **[P1]** `determinism.rs`

49: pub struct FiniteScore(f64);

51: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
52: pub enum ScoreError {
53:     #[error("score must be finite")]
54:     NonFinite,
55: }
56: 
57: impl TryFrom<f64> for FiniteScore {
58:     type Error = ScoreError;
59: 
60:     fn try_from(value: f64) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
61:         if !value.is_finite() {
62:             return Err(ScoreError::NonFinite);
63:         }
64: 
65:         Ok(Self(value))

122: | `From<T>` | Infallible, lossless, value-preserving conversion | P1 |
123: | `TryFrom<T>` | Validation, narrowing, parsing, or normalization can fail | P1 |
124: | `AsRef<T>` | Cheap borrowed view | P2 |
125: | `IntoIterator` | Natural collection traversal without ABI exposure | P2 |
126: | `as` cast | Only a reviewed conversion proven not to narrow or alter semantics | P0 |
127: | Public builder | Avoid at JS/WASM boundary | P1 |
128: 
129: - **[P1]** Implement `From` or `TryFrom`, not `Into` or `TryInto`, directly.
130: - **[P0]** Do not use `as` for boundary narrowing.
131: - **[P1]** Use complete options DTOs at JavaScript boundaries.
132: - **[P2]** Use builders only for genuinely complex internal construction.
133: - **[P2]** Use type-state only when it prevents a real invalid transition.
134: - **[P0]** Keep builders and type-state representations out of the exported ABI.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## 3. STANDARD COLLECTION AND SERIALIZATION TYPES
139: 
140: ### Collection Selection
141: 
142: **[P1] Prefer standard collections and make observable ordering explicit.**
143: 
144: | Requirement | Type | Severity | Notes |
145: |-------------|------|----------|-------|
146: | Sequence preserving explicit order | `Vec<T>` | P1 | Canonicalize before export |
147: | Canonical key order | `BTreeMap<K, V>` | P0 | Preferred for parity-visible maps |
148: | Canonical unique values | `BTreeSet<T>` | P0 | Ordered deduplication |
149: | Deterministic insertion order | `IndexMap<K, V>` | P1 | Use only when insertion order is contractual |
150: | Internal unordered lookup | `HashMap<K, V>` | P1 | Never leak iteration order |
151: | Internal unordered membership | `HashSet<T>` | P1 | Never leak iteration order |
152: | FIFO work queue | `VecDeque<T>` | P2 | Use when queue operations are material |
153: 
154: ### Observable Hash Iteration
155: 
156: **[P0] `HashMap` and `HashSet` iteration must never influence output, serialization, hashing, deterministic IDs, traversal order, or ranking.** This protects **deterministic iteration and serialized-output parity**.
157: 
158: ```rust
159: use std::collections::HashMap;
160: 
161: pub fn canonical_entries(
162:     values: &HashMap<String, u32>,
163: ) -> Vec<(&str, u32)> {
164:     let mut entries: Vec<_> = values
165:         .iter()
166:         .map(|(key, value)| (key.as_str(), *value))
167:         .collect();
168: 
169:     entries.sort_by(|left, right| left.0.cmp(right.0));
170:     entries
171: }
172: ```
173: 
174: - **[P0]** Do not rely on a deterministic hasher to make hash-table iteration contractual.
175: - **[P0]** Do not rely on input insertion order unless the contract explicitly defines it.
176: - **[P1]** Collect and sort unordered data before any observable operation.
177: - **[P1]** Prefer `BTreeMap` when canonical key order is always required.
178: 
179: ### Serialization DTOs
180: 
181: **[P0] Boundary DTOs are passive, owned, and versioned.** Serialization must preserve the TypeScript contract for field names, field order, omission, nullability, escaping, encoding, and number spelling.
182: 
183: ```rust
184: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
185: 
186: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
187: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
188: pub struct SearchResultDto {
189:     pub id: String,
190:     pub score: f64,
191:     pub text: String,
192:     #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
193:     pub explanation: Option<String>,
194: }
195: ```
196: 
197: - **[P0]** Verify that `skip_serializing_if` matches TypeScript omission behavior.
198: - **[P0]** Do not use `Option<T>` without testing missing, `null`, and present cases.
199: - **[P0]** Do not flatten structures unless the TypeScript schema already does so.
200: - **[P0]** Do not accept unknown fields silently when the established TypeScript validator rejects them.
201: - **[P1]** Use explicit serde attributes for JavaScript-visible names.
202: - **[P1]** Convert serialized DTOs to private core types before processing.
203: 
204: ### Canonical Serialization
205: 
206: **[P0] Generic `serde_json::to_string` is not automatically a TypeScript-compatible serializer.** It may differ in key order, number spelling, escaping, or omission behavior. This protects **serialized-output parity**.
207: 
208: ```rust
209: use serde::Serialize;
210: 
211: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
212: pub enum CanonicalJsonError {
213:     #[error("failed to serialize canonical output: {0}")]
214:     Serialize(#[from] serde_json::Error),
215: }
216: 
217: pub fn serialize_canonical<T>(
218:     value: &T,
219: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CanonicalJsonError>
220: where
221:     T: Serialize,
222: {
223:     let text = serde_json::to_string(value)?;
224:     Ok(text.into_bytes())
225: }
226: ```
227: 
228: The helper above is acceptable only after fixtures establish that its exact output matches the TypeScript oracle for the relevant DTO.
229: 
230: - **[P0]** Compare serialized bytes without normalization.
231: - **[P0]** Preserve UTF-8 encoding and newline policy.
232: - **[P0]** Preserve object-key order.
233: - **[P0]** Preserve JavaScript number spelling.
234: - **[P0]** Preserve escaping behavior.
235: - **[P0]** Do not use pretty printing unless whitespace is contractual.
236: - **[P1]** Centralize canonical serialization rather than configuring it ad hoc in adapters.
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ## 4. PUBLIC API AND ABI CONTRACTS
241: 
242: ### Explicit Public Signatures
243: 
244: **[P1] Public Rust APIs require explicit parameter, return, and error types.** Public signatures are reviewable contracts and must not change accidentally through inference.
245: 
246: ```rust
247: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
248: pub struct RankRequest {
249:     pub query: String,
250:     pub candidates: Vec<CandidateDto>,
251: }
252: 
253: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
254: pub struct CandidateDto {
255:     pub id: String,
256:     pub score: f64,
257: }
258: 
259: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
260: pub struct RankedCandidateDto {
261:     pub id: String,
262:     pub score: f64,
263:     pub rank: u32,
264: }
265: 
266: pub fn rank_candidates(
267:     request: RankRequest,
268: ) -> Result<Vec<RankedCandidateDto>, RankError> {
269:     rank_validated(request)
270: }
271: ```
272: 
273: - **[P0]** Export owned DTOs only.
274: - **[P0]** Use fixed-width numbers at ABI boundaries.
275: - **[P0]** Preserve JavaScript-visible names and optionality.
276: - **[P0]** Preserve generated TypeScript declaration shapes.
277: - **[P1]** Keep exported functions narrow.
278: - **[P1]** Keep core-only types private to the core crate.
279: - **[P0]** Do not expose Rust implementation details such as lifetimes, iterators, trait objects, or generic builders.
280: 
281: ### napi-rs Contract
282: 
283: **[P0] napi-rs adapters must translate DTOs and errors without duplicating core behavior.** This protects **native-addon and TypeScript parity**.
284: 
285: ```rust
286: use napi_derive::napi;
287: 
288: #[napi(object)]
289: pub struct RankRequestJs {
290:     pub query: String,
291:     pub candidates: Vec<CandidateJs>,
292: }
293: 
294: #[napi(object)]
295: pub struct CandidateJs {
296:     pub id: String,
297:     pub score: f64,
298: }
299: 
300: #[napi(object)]
301: pub struct RankedCandidateJs {
302:     pub id: String,
303:     pub score: f64,
304:     pub rank: u32,
305: }
306: 
307: #[napi(js_name = "rankCandidates")]
308: pub fn rank_candidates_js(
309:     request: RankRequestJs,
310: ) -> napi::Result<Vec<RankedCandidateJs>> {
311:     let core_request = request
312:         .try_into()
313:         .map_err(map_core_error)?;
314: 
315:     rank_candidates(core_request)
316:         .map(|results| results.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect())
317:         .map_err(map_core_error)
318: }
319: ```
320: 
321: - **[P0]** The adapter must not implement scoring, rounding, sorting, hashing, or validation.
322: - **[P0]** Generated declaration names must match the existing TypeScript API.
323: - **[P0]** Native errors must match JavaScript `name`, `code`, `message`, and rejection behavior.
324: - **[P1]** Select and test the lowest supported Node-API level.
325: - **[P1]** Test the oldest claimed Node version.
326: 
327: ### WASM Contract
328: 
329: **[P0] WASM exports must preserve the same DTO and output contract as native exports unless a distinct ABI is explicitly intended.**
330: 
331: ```rust
332: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
333: 
334: #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = rankCandidates)]
335: pub fn rank_candidates_wasm(input: JsValue) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue> {
336:     let request: RankRequestDto = serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(input)
337:         .map_err(|error| boundary_error("E030", error.to_string()))?;
338: 
339:     let ranked = rank_candidates(request.try_into().map_err(map_wasm_error)?)
340:         .map_err(map_wasm_error)?;
341: 
342:     serde_wasm_bindgen::to_value(&ranked)
343:         .map_err(|error| boundary_error("E040", error.to_string()))
344: }
345: ```
346: 
347: - **[P0]** Serializer configuration must be explicit and golden-tested.
348: - **[P0]** WASM traps must not replace established JavaScript errors.
349: - **[P0]** Promise behavior must match the TypeScript contract.
350: - **[P1]** Test the built WASM artifact through its real JavaScript loader.
351: - **[P0]** Do not claim WASM parity from core-only tests.
352: 
353: ### Sidecar Contract
354: 
355: - **[P0]** Sidecar protocols must define framing, encoding, field order, newline behavior, exit codes, and stderr behavior.
356: - **[P0]** Platform-native path formatting must not leak into parity-visible output.
357: - **[P0]** Sidecar process failures must map to stable TypeScript errors.
358: - **[P1]** Use one transport-neutral core shared with native and WASM adapters.
359: - **[P1]** Test the packaged executable, not only a library call.
360: 
361: ### Versioning and Packaging
362: 
363: - **[P0]** Treat DTO and generated declaration changes as ABI changes.
364: - **[P0]** Treat glibc and musl as separate release targets.
365: - **[P1]** Publish exact-version optional platform packages per OS, CPU, and libc target.
366: - **[P0]** Gate root-package publication on complete platform-package publication.
367: - **[P0]** Use one napi-rs packaging system; do not combine incompatible generated and independent loaders.
368: - **[P1]** Prefer napi-rs's generated WASI fallback when preserving the native Node-facing API.
369: - **[P0]** Treat native and WASI as independent release targets.
370: - **[P0]** Introduce `cxx` only for a concrete C++ dependency and prohibit cross-boundary unwinding.
371:

13: # Domain Modeling, Collections & Public API/ABI Contracts
14: 
15: Ownership, safety, interop, error handling, async patterns, Cargo baseline, and byte-for-byte TypeScript parity standards for Rust in the OpenCode development environment.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Defines the domain types, collection choices and public API and ABI shapes that make Rust state explicit and every exported contract reviewable.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Modeling a parity-sensitive primitive or a state machine
28: - Choosing a collection or a serialization DTO
29: - Designing or reviewing a public Rust API or an ABI contract for napi-rs, WASM or a sidecar
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. DOMAIN AND STATE MODELING
34: 
35: ### Newtypes for Parity-Sensitive Values
36: 
37: **[P1] Use private-field newtypes when primitive values carry distinct validation or parity semantics.**
38: 
39: Appropriate examples include:
40: 
41: - **[P1]** `SymbolId` for deterministic identifiers
42: - **[P1]** `SkillId` for validated identifiers
43: - **[P1]** `FiniteScore` for finite numeric values
44: - **[P1]** `Rank` where zero-based and one-based values must not mix
45: - **[P1]** `ErrorCode` for stable JavaScript error codes
46: 
47: ```rust
48: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
49: pub struct FiniteScore(f64);
50: 
51: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
52: pub enum ScoreError {
53:     #[error("score must be finite")]
54:     NonFinite,
55: }
56: 
57: impl TryFrom<f64> for FiniteScore {
58:     type Error = ScoreError;
59: 
60:     fn try_from(value: f64) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
61:         if !value.is_finite() {
62:             return Err(ScoreError::NonFinite);
63:         }
64: 
65:         Ok(Self(value))
66:     }
67: }
68: 
69: impl FiniteScore {
70:     pub fn get(self) -> f64 {
71:         self.0
72:     }
73: }
74: ```
75: 
76: - **[P0]** Reject non-finite values unless the boundary contract explicitly defines their encoding.
77: - **[P0]** Normalize or preserve `-0.0` according to the TypeScript oracle.
78: - **[P1]** Keep fields private so invalid values cannot be constructed directly.
79: - **[P1]** Serialize newtypes to the existing TypeScript primitive representation.
80: - **[P2]** Implement common traits only where their semantics are valid.
81: 
82: ### State as Enums
83: 
84: **[P1] Model mutually exclusive states with enums rather than independent booleans.** This protects **domain-state validity and discriminant parity**.
85: 
86: ```rust
87: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
88: pub enum ConnectionState {
89:     Disconnected,
90:     Connecting { attempt: u32 },
91:     Connected { endpoint: String },
92:     Failed { code: String, message: String },
93: }
94: 
95: pub fn connection_summary(state: &ConnectionState) -> String {
96:     match state {
97:         ConnectionState::Disconnected => "Not connected".to_owned(),
98:         ConnectionState::Connecting { attempt } => {
99:             format!("Connecting (attempt {attempt})")
100:         }
101:         ConnectionState::Connected { endpoint } => {
102:             format!("Connected to {endpoint}")
103:         }
104:         ConnectionState::Failed { code, message } => {
105:             format!("Error {code}: {message}")
106:         }
107:     }
108: }
109: ```
110: 
111: - **[P0]** Export enums using stable string discriminants or explicit numeric codes.
112: - **[P0]** Never expose incidental Rust ordinal values as the JavaScript contract.
113: - **[P1]** Map every exported discriminant explicitly in adapters.
114: - **[P0]** Treat an unhandled adapter variant as a compile-time failure, not a wildcard fallback.
115: - **[P1]** Use `#[non_exhaustive]` only when wildcard evolution is intentional.
116: - **[P0]** Do not use `#[non_exhaustive]` to hide missing error or ABI mappings.
117: 
118: ### Conversion Policies
119: 
120: | Conversion | Use | Severity |
121: |------------|-----|----------|
122: | `From<T>` | Infallible, lossless, value-preserving conversion | P1 |
123: | `TryFrom<T>` | Validation, narrowing, parsing, or normalization can fail | P1 |
124: | `AsRef<T>` | Cheap borrowed view | P2 |
125: | `IntoIterator` | Natural collection traversal without ABI exposure | P2 |
126: | `as` cast | Only a reviewed conversion proven not to narrow or alter semantics | P0 |
127: | Public builder | Avoid at JS/WASM boundary | P1 |
128: 
129: - **[P1]** Implement `From` or `TryFrom`, not `Into` or `TryInto`, directly.
130: - **[P0]** Do not use `as` for boundary narrowing.
131: - **[P1]** Use complete options DTOs at JavaScript boundaries.
132: - **[P2]** Use builders only for genuinely complex internal construction.
133: - **[P2]** Use type-state only when it prevents a real invalid transition.
134: - **[P0]** Keep builders and type-state representations out of the exported ABI.

138: ## 3. STANDARD COLLECTION AND SERIALIZATION TYPES
139: 
140: ### Collection Selection
141: 
142: **[P1] Prefer standard collections and make observable ordering explicit.**
143: 
144: | Requirement | Type | Severity | Notes |
145: |-------------|------|----------|-------|

212: pub enum CanonicalJsonError {
213:     #[error("failed to serialize canonical output: {0}")]

215: }
216: 
217: pub fn serialize_canonical<T>(
218:     value: &T,
219: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CanonicalJsonError>
220: where
221:     T: Serialize,
222: {
223:     let text = serde_json::to_string(value)?;
224:     Ok(text.into_bytes())

226: ```

232: - **[P0]** Preserve object-key order.
233: - **[P0]** Preserve JavaScript number spelling.
234: - **[P0]** Preserve escaping behavior.
235: - **[P0]** Do not use pretty printing unless whitespace is contractual.
236: - **[P1]** Centralize canonical serialization rather than configuring it ad hoc in adapters.

240: ## 4. PUBLIC API AND ABI CONTRACTS

242: ### Explicit Public Signatures
243: 
244: **[P1] Public Rust APIs require explicit parameter, return, and error types.** Public signatures are reviewable contracts and must not change accidentally through inference.
245:

248: pub struct RankRequest {

275: - **[P0]** Preserve JavaScript-visible names and optionality.

328:

330: 
331: ```rust

333: 
334: #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = rankCandidates)]
335: pub fn rank_candidates_wasm(input: JsValue) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue> {
336:     let request: RankRequestDto = serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(input)

339:     let ranked = rank_candidates(request.try_into().map_err(map_wasm_error)?)

21:

23:

25:

29:

33:     rust_boundary(input)?.as_bytes(),
34: );
35: ```
36:

38: 
39: ### When to Use
40:

42: - Adding napi-rs, wasm-bindgen, WASI, or sidecar adapters

44: - Defining Rust DTOs, errors, serialization, or public exports
45: - Configuring Cargo, Clippy, rustfmt, MSRV, or supply-chain gates

47: - Evaluating async, threading, zero-copy, or unsafe optimizations
48: 
49: 
50: ### Severity Levels
51: 
52: | Level | Meaning | Enforcement |
53: |-------|---------|-------------|
54: | **P0** | Hard blocker affecting safety, ABI compatibility, process survival, or byte parity | Must be corrected before merge or release |
55: | **P1** | Required engineering standard | Must be satisfied unless a narrow, reviewed exception is documented |
56: | **P2** | Recommended quality improvement | Apply when relevant; record why it is deferred when omission is material |
57:

This protects **DTO/ABI and JavaScript error-shape parity**.

This protects **six-decimal score parity, stable sort parity, deterministic-ID parity, deterministic iteration order, and serialized-output parity**.
62: - **[P0] No `unsafe` is permitted without a documented invariant and tests.** The pure core forbids unsafe code. Every permitted boundary unsafe block requires an adjacent `// SAFETY:` explanation, an exercising test, and a precondition-challenge test. This protects **FFI memory safety and boundary integrity**.
63: - **[P0] Panics are not boundary errors.** JavaScript-controlled input must not reach `unwrap`, `expect`, unchecked indexing, explicit `panic!`, or assertion-dependent validation. This protects **Node process survival, WASM trap avoidance, and JavaScript error-shape parity**.
64: - **[P0] TypeScript remains the behavior authority.** MCP transport, public tool schemas, daemon and CLI wiring, feature flags, and fallback selection remain in TypeScript. Rust adapters expose only narrow, measured kernels. This protects **transport compatibility and fallback behavior**.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 2. OWNED VS BORROWED DATA DECISION GUIDE
69: 
70: ### Boundary Rule
71: 
72: **[P0] Export owned, materialized values across JavaScript, WASM, sidecar, thread, and async boundaries.** Borrowed data must not outlive the Rust call frame or depend on JavaScript garbage-collector reachability. This protects **buffer ownership and ABI lifetime integrity**.
73: 
74: Approved boundary types include:
75: 
76: - **[P1]** `String`
77: - **[P1]** `Vec<T>`
78: - **[P1]** Fixed-width integers such as `u32`, `i64`, and `u64`
79: - **[P1]** `f64` with explicit finite-value and parity validation
80: - **[P1]** `bool`
81: - **[P1]** Owned DTO structs
82: - **[P1]** `Option<OwnedType>`
83: - **[P1]** `Result<OwnedOutput, BoundaryError>`
84: 
85: Do not export:
86: 
87: - **[P0]** `&str` or `&[T]`
88: - **[P0]** DTO fields containing references
89: - **[P0]** Public lifetime parameters
90: - **[P0]** `Cow<'a, T>` across the boundary
91: - **[P0]** Iterators or closures
92: - **[P0]** Internal graph references
93: - **[P0]** Rust builders or type-state values
94: - **[P0]** `usize` or `isize`
95: - **[P0]** JavaScript handles captured by background work
96: 
97: ### Decision Summary
98: 
99: | Situation | Preferred Form | Severity | Contract Protected |
100: |-----------|----------------|----------|--------------------|
101: | Core helper reads text temporarily | `&str` | P1 | Allocation clarity |
102: | Core helper reads a slice temporarily | `&[T]` | P1 | Allocation clarity |
103: | napi-rs or WASM input DTO | Owned struct | P0 | Boundary lifetime integrity |
104: | Async or cross-thread input | Owned, `Send + 'static` data | P0 | Thread and runtime safety |
105: | Returned text or bytes | `String` or `Vec<u8>` | P0 | ABI ownership |
106: | Optional JS field | `Option<T>` with verified omission/null mapping | P0 | DTO parity |
107: | Integer boundary value | Fixed-width integer plus range validation | P0 | Cross-platform ABI parity |
108: | Internal read-only alternate representation | `Cow<'_, T>` | P2 | Allocation efficiency |
109: | Synchronous zero-copy view | Reviewed exception with explicit lifetime proof | P0 | Memory safety |
110: 
111: ### Borrow Internally, Own at Boundaries
112: 
113: **[P1] Borrow within the pure core when the caller controls the lifetime.** This avoids unnecessary allocation without exposing lifetime coupling through the ABI.
114: 
115: ```rust
116: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
117: pub struct NormalizedQuery(String);
118: 
119: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
120: pub enum QueryError {
121:     #[error("query must not be empty")]
122:     Empty,
123: }
124: 
125: impl NormalizedQuery {
126:     pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Self, QueryError> {
127:         let normalized = input.trim().to_lowercase();
128: 
129:         if normalized.is_empty() {
130:             return Err(QueryError::Empty);
131:         }
132: 
133:         Ok(Self(normalized))
134:     }
135: 
136:     pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
137:         &self.0
138:     }
139: 
140:     pub fn into_string(self) -> String {
141:         self.0
142:     }
143: }
144: ```
145: 
146: - **[P1]** Use `as_*` for cheap borrowed views.
147: - **[P1]** Use `to_*` for conversions that perform work or allocate.
148: - **[P1]** Use `into_*` for consuming conversions.
149: - **[P1]** Convert boundary DTOs into validated core types immediately.
150: 
151: ### Owned Boundary Conversion
152: 
153: **[P1] Use `TryFrom` for boundary validation.** Fallible conversion must not be hidden inside an infallible `From` implementation. This protects **input-validation and error-shape parity**.

155: ```rust
